extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, representatives and national IP offices interacting with ARIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, prosecuting, publishing, and maintaining ARIPO patents, utility models and industrial designs, including examination, appeals, re-establishment of rights, and special requirements (e.g., micro-organisms, medical claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing for ARIPO utility model application
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO utility model application shall be published as soon as possible—(a) after the expiry of a period of 18 months from the date of filing or, if priority has been claimed, from the date of priority; or (b) at the request of the applicant, before the expiry of the 18-month period and subject to the payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the decision to register the utility model becomes effective before the expiry of the 18-month period, the application shall be published at the same time as the specification. For priority claims, the 18 months is calculated from the original filing date (or earliest priority date if multiple claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application content
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the registration of an industrial design shall contain a request for registration of an industrial design and a reproduction of the industrial design, and be subject to the payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal content requirements (request and reproduction) are mandatory to obtain a filing date and for further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination of industrial design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine whether the formal requirements for applications have been complied with and, if so, shall accord the appropriate filing date to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office finds non-compliance it shall notify the applicant inviting compliance within the prescribed period; failure to comply leads to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of designated States on industrial design filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall notify each designated State that an application for the registration of an industrial design has been filed which complies with the prescribed formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers the designated States' 6-month period to make written communications concerning territorial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and timing for designated State communications (industrial designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expiration of 6 months from notification each designated State may communicate that, if registered by the Office, the registration shall have no effect in its territory for the reason that (i) the industrial design is not new, (ii) because of the nature of the industrial design it cannot be registered or a registration has no effect under the national law, or (iii) in the case of a textile design, it is the subject of a special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such a communication is made the applicant may respond with amendments and/or arguments within the prescribed period; designated States must respond within the prescribed period. If refusal persists applicant may request treatment as a national application in that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and publication of industrial design registration after 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: After the expiration of the 6 months, the Office shall effect the registration of the industrial design, which shall have effect in those designated States which have not made the communication referred to in the 6-month procedure, and the Office shall publish the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated States that made no adverse communication are bound by the ARIPO registration effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal remedy: request for national treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office refuses the application, the applicant may, within 3 months from being notified of such refusal, request that his application be treated, in any designated State, as an application according to the national law of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a route to pursue protection at national offices after ARIPO refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual maintenance fees and duration of industrial design registration
rubrics_metrics.description: On the anniversary of the filing the Office shall collect the prescribed annual maintenance fees; the amount depends on the number of States for which the application/registration is maintained. The duration of such a registration shall be 15 years from the filing date, except for designated States with a shorter term of protection, in which case the registration shall expire at the end of that shorter term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are distributed among designated States as provided in the Regulations; pre-amendment registrations follow former terms where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of national compulsory-licence/use-in-public-interest law to ARIPO-registered industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design registered by the Office shall in each designated State be subject to the provisions of the applicable national law on compulsory licences or the use in the public interest of registered industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO registration does not override national provisions allowing compulsory use/licences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Appeal composition and quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Appeal shall consist of five members experienced in intellectual property matters, two of whom shall be patent examiners. At all sittings of the Board at least one patent examiner shall be present. Three members form a quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members appointed by Administrative Council for 2 years renewable once; membership from Member States; Council sets terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Appeal functions and decision finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The functions of the Board are to consider and decide on any appeal lodged by the applicant in terms of Section 3(5), to review any final administrative decision of the Office in relation to implementation of this Protocol (and related protocols), and to decide on other matters related to its powers. Decisions of the Board shall be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may make and adopt its own rules of procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations-making power and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council of ARIPO shall make Regulations for the implementation of this Protocol and may amend them where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations shall relate in particular to administrative requirements, matters of procedure, details necessary for implementation of the Protocol and relevant international treaties, and fees to be charged and distribution details among Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-establishment of rights (restoration) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or proprietor who, in spite of all due care required by the circumstances having been taken, was unable to observe a time limit, shall have his rights re-established upon request if the non-observance has the direct consequence of causing refusal of the ARIPO application or request, deeming the application withdrawn, or loss of any other right or means of redress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO shall grant the request provided conditions and Implementing Regulations requirements are met; if granted the legal consequences are deemed not to have ensued. Re-establishment is ruled out for the time limit for requesting re-establishment; no right is deemed re-established until the request is granted. Implementing Regulations may rule out re-establishment of other time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of third-party good-faith users upon re-establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, in a designated Contracting State, has in good faith used or made effective and serious preparations for using an invention or design subject to a published ARIPO application or ARIPO right in the period between the loss of rights and publication of the mention of re-establishment, may without payment continue such use in the course of his business or for the needs thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards bona fide third parties who relied on the lapse prior to re-establishment publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for limitation (post-grant amendment) filing and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the proprietor, the ARIPO patent or utility model may be limited by an amendment; the request shall be filed in accordance with Implementing Regulations and shall not be deemed filed until the limitation fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment to the claims must fall wholly within the scope of the claims before the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force and accession formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State a member of the Organization or to which membership is open may become party by signature followed by deposit of instrument of ratification or deposit of instrument of accession; instruments are deposited with Director General. Protocol enters into force 3 months after 3 States deposit instruments; subsequent accessions bind States 3 months after deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratification/accession entails acceptance of the Agreement on the Creation of ARIPO; deposit of instruments may have effect in making State party to Agreement on deposit date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may denounce the Protocol by notification to the Director General. Denunciation takes effect 6 months after receipt; it shall not affect any patent application or application for registration filed with the Office prior to the expiry of the 6-month period or any patent granted or registration effected upon such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects pending filings and recently granted rights from being affected by denunciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers and Journal maintenance and publication frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall maintain a Patents Register, a Utility Models Register and an Industrial Designs Register recording particulars provided in these Regulations. The Office shall publish a Journal in which it effects all publications provided for in the Protocol and Regulations; the Journal shall be published at least monthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording of granted patents is effected by inserting a copy; other recordings are effected under appropriate headings as facts or instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of files and pre-publication confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (2) any person may, upon payment of the prescribed fee, consult the Registers or obtain copies. Files relating to ARIPO patent, utility model and industrial design applications which have not yet been published shall not be made available for inspection and extracts obtained without the written consent of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even before grant, the Office shall, on request, communicate certain bibliographic data (applicant/agent name and addresses, application number, filing and priority dates, title, changes in ownership and licence references). If an application is withdrawn before publication, file inspection requires permission and the bibliographic communications do not apply. Courts/authorities may obtain copies of relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information services mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall provide, upon request, patent information services to users of patent information in Member States and potential Member States of ARIPO for the purpose of facilitating adaptation, transfer and acquisition of appropriate technology, development of local research and creation of indigenous technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office acts as information resource to support technology development in Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an ARIPO patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for a patent shall contain: (a) a request; (b) a description; (c) one or more claims; (d) one or more drawings (where necessary); (e) an abstract; (f) a designation of the Contracting States in respect of which the patent is requested to be granted; and (g) sequence listing if patent application contains disclosure of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences (submitted in electronic form conforming to WIPO ST.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness of these elements is necessary for proper filing and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be in the English language and any document forming part of the application and which is in a language other than English shall be accompanied by an English translation certified by the applicant or the person having translated the application in a statement that the translation is a correct record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures ARIPO procedures operate in a single working language (English) with certified translations when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request form contents and checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The printed request form shall contain a list which when filled in shows total number of sheets constituting the application and the number of sheets of each element, whether the application is accompanied by power of attorney, priority document, fee receipt or undertaking to pay fees, statement justifying applicant's right to the patent and other documents, and the number of the most illustrative drawing suggested to accompany the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant fills the list; if not, the Office will fill and annotate. Request must be signed and contain prescribed petition and specified personal and representative details; title should be short (preferably 2-7 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, title and applicant/representative/inventor particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall be signed by the applicant and contain a petition, the title of the invention (short and precise), the name/address/nationality of the applicant; name/address/place of business of representative; where applicant is not inventor a statement specifying basis of applicant's right; and where applicable a declaration of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses must satisfy customary requirements for prompt postal delivery and names of natural persons indicated family name before given name(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing permissibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent, industrial design and utility model applications may be filed and processed in electronic form or by electronic means in accordance with Administrative Instructions provided that the Office or any Member States’ office shall permit filing on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions set acknowledgement of receipt, filing date procedures, physical requirements, consequences of non-compliance, signature and authentication procedures. Member States need notify ARIPO to accept e-filings; notified States cannot refuse compliant electronic filings. Rule applies mutatis mutandis to other correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description requirements (enablement, background, best mode, industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall: (a) state the title of the invention; (b) specify the technical field; (c) indicate the background art useful for understanding/searching/examination, preferably citing documents; (d) disclose the invention in such terms that it can be understood and state its advantageous effects with reference to background art; (e) briefly describe the figures; (f) set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention (in terms of examples where appropriate and with reference to drawings); and (g) indicate explicitly, when not obvious, the way the invention is industrially applicable and how it can be made and used, or if only used, how it can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specified manner and order shall be followed except when a different order better suits understanding and conciseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-organism deposit requirement for enabling disclosure (Rule 6bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If performance of an invention requires use of a micro-organism that is not publicly available at filing date and cannot be so described as to enable performance by a skilled person, the description shall be regarded as disclosing the invention only if not later than the date of filing a culture has been deposited with an international depositary institution, and the application gives the depository's name, deposit date and file number (and new deposits must be made as required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information is not in the application as filed, it must be submitted before the end of 16 months after filing or priority date, or earlier when prompted by an Office communication on third-party requests. Submission constitutes consent for the depository to make the culture available on appropriate certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of deposited micro-organism culture to requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposited culture shall be available upon request to any person from the date of publication of the ARIPO patent application and to any person entitled to inspect files prior to that date, provided the requester undertakes: (a) not to make the culture or derived cultures available to third parties before refusal/withdrawal or patent expiry; and (b) to use the culture or derived culture for experimental purposes only until refusal/withdrawal/publication of grant (does not apply where requester uses culture under a compulsory licence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability is effected by issuing a sample and is mediated by Office certification to the depository and applicant/proprietor notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of deposited culture to nominated experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Until publication the applicant may require that availability of the culture be effected only by the issue of a sample to an expert nominated by the requester. The expert may be a natural person with applicant approval or a person recognised by the Director General; nomination must be accompanied by an undertaking similar to that required of requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides controlled access to protect applicant's interests while allowing expert inspection for examination purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for new deposit where original culture becomes unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deposited micro-organism ceases to be available (non-viability or other reason) and has not been transferred to another recognised institution, an interruption in availability is deemed not to have occurred if a new deposit is made within 3 months from notification of interruption and a copy of the new deposit receipt forwarded to the Office within 4 months, stating the application/patent number; new deposit location rules depend on cause and recognition status of institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where institution ceases to be recognised, timing triggers may be based on Journal announcement; any new deposit must include a depositor's statement that the newly deposited micro-organism is the same as originally deposited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims drafting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought in terms of the technical features of the invention; they shall be clear and concise and be supported by the description. The number of claims shall be reasonable, and where several claims exist they shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, claims shall contain (a) a statement indicating technical features necessary for definition but which are part of the prior art; and (b) a characterizing portion (preceded by 'characterized in that', 'characterized by', 'wherein the improvement comprises' or similar) stating concisely the technical features desired to be protected. Claims should not, except where absolutely necessary, rely on references to the description or drawings (e.g., 'as described in part...' or 'as illustrated in figure...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of medical indication/use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims related to medical indications or use claims shall, for the purpose of examination, be drafted in accordance with standard phrases provided (examples include: 'Pharmaceutical composition for the prophylaxis/treatment of Y comprising X', 'Compound X for use as a drug/medicament for the treatment of Y', 'Use of X for the manufacture of a pharmaceutical composition', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct sets of standard formulations are provided for first medical indications and second medical indications (e.g., 'Use of X for the manufacture of a medicament for treatment of Y'). Use these standard phrasings in drafting to comply with ARIPO examination practice.
